title: Rav Sheva
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned in Horayot 5b: he raised a difficulty against Rav Kahana.
We also find Rav bar Sheva in Berakhot 11, Rava bar Sheva in Shabbat 140, or Ravin bar Sheva in Chullin 48.
Rav Shmuel bar Sheva in Shevuot 17b.

notes.text: The heading’s שבא differs from the parenthetical biblical שבע. The printed Genesis 25:13 reference remains a source question.

The saved whole Masorah Genesis25:3 verse names Sheba, spelled שבא, son of Yokshan. Supplied parenthesis spells שבע and cites25:13; both remain beside the matching verse, without asserting verified print errors. The biblical name is a namesake pointer, not identification of Rav Sheva. Supplied Berakhot11, Shabbat140 and Chullin48 lack explicit amud markers, so the earlier blanket a-side additions are withdrawn. Horayot5b and Shevuot17b have explicit colons. Full Rav titles are supplied in this notice; no genealogy is newly admitted.

The parenthesis in the print (vol. III, p. 1108) gives שבא and Genesis 25:3, where the supplied Hebrew transcription gives שבע and 25:13. The verse at 25:3 names Sheba son of Yokshan. In the Bavli, the consulted readings give Rav Shaba questioning Rav Kahana at Horayot 5b, Rava bar Sheva at Shabbat 140a, Ravin bar Sheva at Chullin 48a and Rav Shmuel bar Sheva at Shevuot 17b. Hyman cites Berakhot 11 for Rav bar Sheva. A passage naming Rav bar Sheva visiting Ravina is at Berakhot 14a in the consulted edition. These notices do not establish that the similarly named sages were the same person.
